title: Startup Recruiter Costs: Fractional vs Agency vs Full-Time
summary: Compare ATS with fractional recruiter costs versus agencies and full-time hires. Setup guidance and hiring thresholds for November 2026.
body_markdown:
Hiring gets messy when your tools and people aren’t aligned. One system tracks candidates, another holds recruiter activity, and you’re left piecing together what’s actually happening. An[ATS with fractional recruiter](https://www.dover.com/) support can help by bringing both sides into the same workflow, where sourcing, outreach, and feedback can live in one place from the start. Your team can stay focused on decisions while the recruiter handles the agreed tasks.


**TLDR:**


- Fractional recruiters can work inside your ATS for shared visibility; hourly fees depend on hours worked, while agency fees depend on the agreed salary percentage.
- Free ATS software paired with fractional recruiting can cover infrastructure and capacity without fixed overhead.
- Fractional recruiting often suits startups making 5-50 hires yearly; full-time may make sense around 15-20 annual hires.
- Shared candidate pipelines can reduce duplicate outreach when everyone records activity consistently.
- Some solutions combine a free ATS with vetted fractional recruiters for startups hiring without headcount commitment.


## What a Fractional Recruiter Does within Your ATS


When an agency works in a separate system, visibility can depend on agreed reporting and update schedules. That setup may suit teams outsourcing a search, but it can leave hiring managers without a shared view of day-to-day recruiting activity.


A fractional recruiter can work inside your applicant tracking system alongside your team instead of running a separate process. Sourced candidates, outreach, status changes, and notes can stay in one place, reducing the need for separate spreadsheets and status calls.


In practice, a[fractional recruiter](https://www.dover.com/blog/what-is-fractional-recruiter-when-startup-needs-one) embedded in your ATS typically owns sourcing, outreach, screening, and interview coordination within the same system. Your team can follow progress when records stay current.


## Why Startups Pair Free ATS Tools with Fractional Recruiting


Most early-stage startups face the same tension: hiring is urgent, but budgets are thin and headcount needs change month to month. For full-time recruiter budgeting, the[BLS wage data for human resources specialists](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/business-and-financial/human-resources-specialists.htm) offers a starting point, though wages are not the same as loaded costs, which also include benefits and overhead. SPECTRAFORCE’s May 2025 guide puts typical direct-hire agency fees at[15-25% of first-year salary](https://spectraforce.com/blogs/how-much-do-staffing-agencies-charge-for-direct-hire/) . Either model may suit steady hiring or a difficult search, but the cost structure matters when hiring demand shifts quarter to quarter.


Free ATS software can cover hiring infrastructure without a software subscription when its features meet your needs.[Fractional recruiting can add capacity](https://www.lloydstaffing.com/fractional-recruiting/) , with commitments depending on the agreement. Together, they can support both sides of the equation when the software and recruiter scope fit the work.


The pairing also follows a clear division of labor. An ATS holds the hiring infrastructure: job postings, pipeline stages, candidate records, and interview feedback. It does not source passive candidates, write outreach, or screen applicants on its own. Self-serve hiring can work well when inbound applications are strong and your team has time to review them. When sourcing gets harder or no one has recruiting bandwidth, a fractional recruiter can add that capacity inside the same system. Because the structure already exists, the recruiter can often start on candidates sooner instead of building process first.


## Cost Comparison: Fractional Recruiters vs Traditional Agency Fees


Under a percentage-based agency agreement, the fee rises with the accepted salary, tying recruiting spend to compensation instead of hours worked.


[Hourly fractional recruiting](https://www.dover.com/blog/fractional-recruiter-costs) uses a different basis: total fee depends on hours worked and the agreed rate, not salary. Retainers and success fees are other options.


Model Fee Structure Cost Basis


Traditional Agency Typically 15-25% of salary $18,000-$30,000 on a $120K hire


Fractional Recruiter Hourly engagement Varies with hours worked and agreed rate


Full-Time Recruiter Annual loaded cost Estimated $85,000-$170,000/year, spread across annual hires


[SHRM’s 2025 benchmarking release](https://www.shrm.org/about/press-room/shrm-releases-2025-benchmarking-reports--how-does-your-organizat) reports higher average hiring costs for executive roles than nonexecutive roles. These benchmarks offer context, but total cost per hire and an outside recruiter’s fee are different measures, best compared when seniority and search complexity are accounted for.


## When Fractional Recruiting Makes More Sense Than a Full-Time Hire


Hiring volume is one useful signal. If you’re filling 5-50 roles a year, a fractional recruiter can often cover the work without full-time overhead, depending on role complexity and hours agreed.


Seed to Series C startups may land in that middle range, with hiring needs that spike during a fundraise and slow during a product crunch. That variability can make a full-time annual commitment hard to support when heavy recruiting support is only needed for part of the year.


A useful rule of thumb:[consider a full-time recruiter](https://www.dover.com/blog/fractional-recruiter-vs-full-time-recruiter-which-is-right-for-your-startup) once you’re consistently making 15 to 20 or more hires per year. Below that, fractional support can offer relevant expertise with less fixed cost.


## ATS Features That Matter Most for Fractional Recruiting Teams


Not every ATS feature matters equally when a fractional recruiter is involved; a few are load-bearing.


The ones that count:


- Shared candidate pipelines so the recruiter and your team see the same stages and status, cutting reliance on update emails.
- Activity logs tracking who sourced whom, which helps reduce duplicate outreach.
- Centralized notes and feedback so interview impressions stay in one place instead of scattered inboxes.
- Job board distribution the recruiter can manage directly without a separate login.
- AI-assisted applicant scoring that helps triage inbound volume, with human review of decisions.


Avoid an ATS that forces the recruiter to work outside the system. A separate tracker means losing the visibility that makes fractional collaboration worth it.


## October 2026 Update: AI Screening Needs Clear Ownership


AI screening raises a compliance question alongside workflow gains: who owns how the tool gets used? Illinois is a clear case. Per[Seyfarth’s June 2026 legal update](https://www.seyfarth.com/news-insights/illinois-department-of-human-rights-temporarily-withdraws-proposed-rules-on-use-of-artificial-intelligence-in-employment.html) , the state’s AI hiring law took effect January 1, 2026, requiring notice for covered AI use and barring discriminatory outcomes. In June, the Illinois Department of Human Rights temporarily withdrew its proposed implementing rules, but the underlying statutory duties remain in effect.


For a founder and fractional recruiter sharing an ATS, agree early who reviews AI-assisted screening, who sends candidate notices, and where decision notes live. Shared records help, but software alone does not make a process compliant. AI scores can support human judgment, not replace it; check current rules with legal counsel before using screening tools.


## How ATS Integration Can Reduce Duplicate Outreach and Candidate Confusion


When multiple tools are in play, the same candidate can get contacted more than once about the same role, and that kind of disorganized outreach can quietly hurt how people perceive your company before an interview happens.


A shared ATS can reduce this when everyone logs outreach and checks records before making contact. Activity logs can attach touchpoints, who reached out, when, and through which channel, to the candidate record, so anyone checking that profile can see the history. Missing records or duplicate profiles can still lead to repeated outreach.


## Setting Up Your Free ATS before Engaging a Fractional Recruiter


Configuring your applicant tracking system before a fractional recruiter joins can save time. A recruiter who walks into a blank system may need to build process before recruiting begins.


A few things worth setting up first:


- Post clear job descriptions and distribute them to relevant job boards so candidates can start applying.
- Define interview stages that reflect your actual hiring process, not a generic template.
- Set up a careers page so candidates can apply before your recruiter starts, building an initial pool.
- Decide which stages your team owns versus what you’re handing off, so there’s no overlap or confusion.


That last point matters most: clear handoff points let the recruiter start sourcing and screening sooner.

## FAQs


### What’s the difference between hourly fractional recruiting and a traditional agency fee for startups?


Hourly fractional recruiting ties your total cost to time worked at an agreed rate, not to the candidate’s accepted salary. Traditional agency fees typically run 15-25% of first-year compensation, so a $120,000 hire can cost $18,000 to $30,000 regardless of how much work the recruiter did. Dover’s marketplace averages roughly $4,800 per hire across all roles.


### Should I set up my ATS before or after engaging a fractional recruiter?


Setting up your ATS first usually helps. A fractional recruiter who joins a configured system, with job postings live, interview stages defined, and a careers page active, can start sourcing and screening sooner instead of building process scaffolding. Deciding which stages your team owns and which the recruiter handles before the engagement starts can also reduce duplicated effort.


### How do I know when to hire a full-time recruiter instead of using fractional recruiting?


A useful threshold is roughly 15 to 20 hires per year on a consistent basis. Below that, a fractional recruiter can often cover the work without full-time overhead, especially when hiring demand fluctuates from quarter to quarter. Seed to Series C startups with variable needs, such as a hiring spike after a fundraise followed by a slower stretch, often fit fractional support better than a fixed annual headcount commitment.


### Do I need a recruiter if I already use an ATS?


Not always. An ATS organizes postings, applicants, and feedback, but someone still has to source, reach out, and screen. If inbound applications cover your roles and your team has time to review them, self-serve hiring may be enough. A fractional recruiter often makes sense when roles are hard to fill, sourcing passive candidates takes more time than your team has, or several searches run at once. Working inside your existing ATS, the recruiter can keep candidates, outreach, and notes in the same pipeline your team follows, which can reduce duplicate outreach and status check-ins.


## Final Thoughts on Choosing an ATS with a Fractional Recruiter for Your Startup


The[ATS with fractional recruiter](https://www.dover.com/) for startups model tends to work best when both sides share one record and the team and recruiter agree early on who owns each stage. The right balance often depends on hiring volume, how much demand swings quarter to quarter, and how much day-to-day visibility you want. Costs and compliance questions, including how AI-assisted screening is reviewed, deserve the same thought as the tools themselves. Dover is one example, pairing a free ATS with vetted fractional recruiters, though external team member access depends on the Premium plan. Good decisions tend to come from judgment about your own hiring rhythm instead of any single benchmark.
